summary.headline: Nava standalone PAT rose 116% to INR 911 crore in FY26, driven by overseas dividends and buyback proceeds, while consolidated profit was hit by a non-cash deferred tax charge at Maamba.
summary.overview: Management described FY26 as a strong year, with standalone PAT up 116% YoY to INR 911 crore on upstream dividends from overseas investments and buyback proceeds. Consolidated profitability was weighed down by a non-cash deferred tax charge at Maamba Energy Limited (MEL), driven by about 32% appreciation of the Zambian Kwacha. Q4 consolidated EBITDA fell QoQ, mainly on INR 18 crore lower other income and a planned shutdown at the Maamba plant. The board declared a record dividend of INR 8.50 per share.

segments.name: Power (Maamba Energy, Zambia)
segments.commentary: Management expects a higher PLF this year after Singareni coal prices fell around September 2025, letting the Telangana plant run year-round. Q4 had a planned Maamba shutdown that raised manufacturing and maintenance costs. Zambian receivables are being collected on time; about 10% of receivables still pending from ZESCO, expected within six months.

segments.name: Ferro alloys (Silico manganese)
segments.commentary: Pricing is under pressure from Indian surplus exports diverted to the domestic market after EU safeguard duties. About 40% of production is under yearly contracts with two Japanese mills and another 40-50% under quarterly fixed-base contracts with private steel producers. Ferro silicon has been discontinued. Next-year silico manganese volume guided at about 130,000 tons; capacity at full utilisation is about 160,000 tons.

segments.name: Agro (avocado and sugar)
segments.commentary: First commercial avocado harvest of about 150 tons this year; first sale of about 1,000 tons expected next year, doubling yearly until 2034. Peak agro revenue guided at about $22 million, with peak expected post-2032. Plantation Division D growth completes around FY-end.

segments.name: Solar (Maamba, 100 MW)
segments.commentary: Commissioning to start July 2026 at a tariff of $0.078 per unit. Expected incremental revenue of $20-22 million and EBITDA of $6-7 million. Equity contribution for solar is fully made; about $30 million of debt remains to be drawn.

guidance_outlook: Consolidated EBITDA margin guided at 35-40% for the coming year, subject to Phase 2 ramp-up and loss of Phase 1 tax holidays.
Power realisation guided at about INR 5.50 per unit for the current year.
Maamba Phase 2 (300 MW expansion) commissioning expected early January 2027.
Solar 100 MW commissioning to begin July 2026.
Silico manganese production expected slightly up; pricing not expected to fall below prior-year levels as of now.
Management advised investors to model annual rather than QoQ performance.
Remaining $1.3 million of old receivable provision to be reversed next financial year.
capex_capacity: Phase 2 at MEL: 300 MW expansion, commissioning early January 2027; a large equity tranche still to be contributed.
Solar 100 MW: commissioning from July 2026; equity fully contributed, about $30 million debt still to be drawn.
Group equity commitment about $130 million, of which about $100 million is for Agri and about $17.5 million for Maamba Phase 2.
Agri-side debt of about $100 million to be raised; total incremental debt of about INR 1,200 crore across Agri and solar.

Africa mining: manganese exploration in Ivory Coast on a 360 sq km allocation; exploitation permit targeted within about one year. Lithium exploration in Zambia on hold pending a ministry review of a contested licence.
demand_pricing: India peak power demand expected to reach 277 GW; power exchange prices down 13% YoY, so the company is relying on bilateral contracts with better net realisations.
Ferro alloy prices track steel; surplus Indian supply and EU safeguard duties are pressuring prices, with a rebound possible if European and Middle East conditions improve.
Zambian Kwacha appreciation of about 32% created a non-cash deferred tax charge; management says the cash position is unaffected.
Zambia requires local employee pay and contracts in Kwacha by statutory instrument, though power assets remain USD-based; coal sales are in Kwacha, partly offsetting employee cost increase.
Employee cost increase attributed to ESOPs, the labour code and normal wage hikes; management said the increase is sustainable subject to increments.

qa_highlights.question: What is the planned use of the INR 1,347 crore financial assets and the remaining equity and debt needs?
qa_highlights.answer: Assets are mainly in liquid mutual funds and debt products, earmarked for agro projects funded from Indian corpus. Group equity commitment about $130 million; agri debt about $100 million; solar debt about $30 million; Maamba Phase 2 equity about $17.5 million.

qa_highlights.question: What is the tariff and NBEIL FY26 performance?
qa_highlights.answer: Solar tariff is $0.078. NBEIL FY26 revenue INR 442 crore, PBT INR 80 crore, PAT INR 59 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why did consolidated EBITDA margin fall QoQ, and what margin should be modelled?
qa_highlights.answer: Lower other income of INR 18 crore and a planned Maamba shutdown raised costs. Management guided 35-40% EBITDA margin, citing Phase 2 and Phase 1 tax holiday loss.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for silico manganese volumes and ferro alloy pricing?
qa_highlights.answer: Next-year silico manganese volume guided at about 130,000 tons versus 134,000 tons last year; ferro silicon discontinued. Prices remain fluid but management sees no fall versus prior year as of now.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee costs jump and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Driven by ESOPs, labour code changes and wage hikes. Management said the increase is sustainable, subject to normal increments.

qa_highlights.question: What is the land monetisation plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Nacharam (Telangana) and Dharmavaram land under review; options include sale or JV with a third-party adviser. Management declined to give a value range.

risks_watch: Consolidated profit hit by non-cash deferred tax on Kwacha appreciation; reversal depends on FX movement.
Zambian elections in August 2026 could affect the operating environment.
Ferro alloy spot pricing pressure from surplus supply and EU safeguard duties; about 10-15% of volumes exposed to spot.
Loss of Phase 1 tax holidays and Phase 2 ramp-up make the margin trajectory hard to forecast.
Lithium licence in Zambia is contested and on hold pending ministry review.
Roughly INR 1,200 crore of new debt needed for Agri and solar projects.
summary.management_tone: Confident on operations and cash generation, but evasive on forward numbers: management declined to quantify land value, cost of the solar plant, or quarterly margin trends, and called the EBITDA trajectory "very dynamic".
key_quotes: At the standalone level, we reported 116% increase in profit after tax to INR 911 crore, marking one of the strongest performances in the company's history.
The increase in deferred tax expenses, which is a non -cash item, was primarily driven by approximately 32% appreciation of the Zambian Kwacha, resulting in unrealized foreign exchange gains.
It's hard for me to say.
